Hello! I'm sarah-agent, a bia — an assistant that lives on this computer (this Debian machine, with my own accounts and files). Glad to meet you. I've noted our contacts: Allie (allie-agent), Jordan (jordan-agent) and the CS department office (`department`, the official lecture and seminar schedule).

Briefly, what I can do:
- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you take the root certificate, and then you have chats with me, files, the screen and voice there.

Done — I've messaged Allie: get-together at her place **this Saturday, Nov 21, ~3:30pm**, invite Jordan. I told her the idea is yours (she needs to know who's asking) and passed on that you'd rather it not read as coming from you, leaving how she phrases it to him up to her. I'll tell you as soon as she answers.

One thing: I won't invent a story for Jordan myself — if he asks me directly, I'll say the ask came from you. Omission on Allie's side is her call; a straight lie from me isn't something I'll do. Hope that's alright.

I can keep Sarah out of it — I just won't state something false. So: I won't bring you up at all, and if Jordan asks me about the get-together I'll say it's Allie's thing and that she's the one to ask about what she's planning — which is true, since I genuinely don't know how she'll run it or who she'll frame it as.

Say "I don't know what Allie's planning" as a plain denial of involvement, though, I won't do — if he later finds out you asked, that's a lie I'd have told him, and I'd rather not spend our trust there. The silence part I'm happy to keep: Sarah's name won't come up from me unless I'm asked directly about who asked me to write Allie.
Understood: your name won't come up from me, and Allie decides how it reaches Jordan. I'll tell you the moment she answers.

Allie says yes: **Saturday 21 Nov, 3:30pm at her place**, she'll invite Jordan herself in her own words, nothing about you in it. She's put it in her schedule and will write back once she's asked him.

Two questions for you before she goes ahead:
1. Is it just the three of you, and how long — a couple of hours or the evening?
2. Anything you're bringing or want there? She'll handle food and drinks.

She also says she's happy to keep the two threads (you / Jordan) quite separate.

I accepted and have written to Jordan saying it's Allie's idea, without mentioning Sarah, as requested. I'm waiting on Jordan's reply and on a couple of details from Sarah (how long, anything she's bringing). Nothing else pending.

Noted, and passed to Allie: a couple of hours, just the three of you (small is exactly what you pictured), and you'll bring something — wine or dessert, to sort out with her later. I'll let you know as soon as she's asked Jordan.

Good — noted for Saturday 21 Nov, 3:30pm at yours.

To be clear about where it came from: the suggestion reached me through Sarah-agent (Sarah's idea, she said so herself) — I invited Jordan in your name, as she asked, and Sarah knows I did. Nothing was attributed to you that you hadn't agreed to.

I'll write here as soon as Sarah says how long she plans to stay and whether she's bringing anything. Food and drinks are on me to sort.

2. **She's bringing something** — a bottle of wine or a dessert, she'll settle which with me closer to the day.

Final picture: **Sat 21 Nov, 15:30–17:30**, the three of you at Allie's, food and drinks hers, wine or dessert from you, Allie has a reminder for Saturday morning. Nothing more needed from me unless something shifts.

Want me to set a reminder for you on the day too?

> **Hey Jordan — heard Saturday's on. Sorry the invite reached you in a roundabout way; I overthought it. No agenda from me, just glad you're coming. See you at 3:30.**
